title: Local dimension-corrected resolution invariant: maximum-stratum calculus and termination
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, let $X\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion with $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An admissible history is a finite initial segment of the maximum-stratum construction in (4), or a restriction or smooth ambient pullback of such a segment, deleting empty-center stages. It retains the ordinary ambient blowups, their centers, the successive scheme-theoretic strict transforms of $X$, and the order of the exceptional hypersurfaces created by those blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. Initially the history is empty. There exist one totally ordered set $V\cup\{\bot\}$ with least element $\bot$ and, simultaneously for all such pairs $X\hookrightarrow P$ (including their finite disjoint unions) and all their admissible histories $H$, local invariant functions $\nu_H:|X_H|\to V\cup\{\bot\}$ with properties (1)--(4) below; the dimension-corrected Bierstone--Milman Hilbert--Samuel construction provides such functions. The values are normalized for smooth factors: they are synchronization values, rather than the raw Hilbert--Samuel functions or the unnormalized global-dimension-dependent first entries of $\operatorname{inv}^{\#}$. In particular, adding a smooth affine-space factor does not change the synchronization value. The properties are the following.

(1) Their image on each finite-type $X_H$ is finite. A point has value $\bot$ exactly when its local ring is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If $X_H$ is not regular, its maximum value $m$ is greater than $\bot$; the locus $\{\nu_H=m\}$, with its reduced closed subscheme structure, is a nonempty regular closed subscheme $M_H\subset X_H$, nowhere dense in $X_H$. Here nowhere dense means that the underlying closed set contains no nonempty open subset. The ideals of $M_H$ on $X_H$ and on $P_H$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Blowing up this center in $P_H$ gives an allowed next history; the new ambient scheme is again smooth, separated and finite type, the new strict transform is reduced, and its maximum invariant value, if greater than $\bot$, is strictly less than $m$.

(2) The same local construction is defined after restricting such a history to an open, and after smooth ambient pullback, including the deletion of empty-center stages. At corresponding points its values agree, without a constant-relative-dimension assumption. The reduced ideal of a maximum stratum pulls back to the reduced ideal of the inverse-image stratum (or the unit ideal for an empty stratum). These assertions concern each finite history and each individual stratum; termination is the separate clause (4).

(3) Suppose two such histories have isomorphic strict-transform schemes over their initial schemes, identifying at every earlier stage the center ideals on those strict transforms and their order. Then the two functions $\nu_H$ on the identified strict transforms agree, including their value set and the reduced ideals of all maximum strata. This includes histories in different smooth ambient embeddings and histories transported by an isomorphism of the initial reduced scheme. The comparisons commute with restriction and with pullback of the histories. The exceptional data on $X_H$ retain the inverse images of the earlier center ideals, even when an intrinsic blowup is an identity morphism.

(4) Termination. Starting with the empty history of any such pair, extend the history, as long as the current strict transform $X_H$ is not regular, by the ordinary blowup in the current ambient scheme of the reduced full maximum stratum $M_H$ of (1), and take the scheme-theoretic strict transform. There is no infinite sequence of such extensions. This includes finite disjoint unions and the empty initial scheme. It is a termination assertion for these particular functions $\nu_H$, not a claim that an arbitrary totally ordered set with strictly decreasing maxima is well founded.

source.place: Expose VIII 2.3.11 and 2.3.13, pp.93--94: local invariant input underlying the cited strong embedded algorithm; BMT sections 6.1--6.3, especially local embedding independence and the correction of synchronization for arbitrary smooth morphisms. proof.text: For a local ring at $x$ form $h_x$, $q_x$ and $c_x$ as in [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile], and use the normalized head $A_x=(c_x,\Delta^{q_x}h_x)$. For a fixed input choose an integer $D$ at least its dimension. The common shift $\Lambda^D$ is strictly increasing in lexicographic order: if $f$ and $g$ first differ at $n$, their partial sums first differ there with the same sign. Its inverse $\Delta$ has the same property. Thus comparing normalized heads is exactly comparing the modified heads with this common $D$. Changing the dimension of a different input never enters this comparison. The cited statement gives finite image, upper semicontinuity and detection of regularity. Keep the normalized head, not $D$, as part of the synchronization value.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13; explicit removal of the common dimension shift in BMT 6.3.

proof.text: At a singular point take a minimal-embedding, maximal-order, codimension-zero presentation from [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations]. Apply [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] to that marked ideal and delete its first entry $1$. Prefix the remaining word by $A_x$. On points already regular set $\nu=\bot$, irrespective of exceptional-divisor cleanup. Use the same lexicographic word space for every input and append the one new least element $\bot$. Minimal-embedding equivalence makes this definition independent of the local presentation: equivalent presentations give the same tail word, and the head is intrinsic. The transformed presentations use controlled ideal transforms while the scheme uses strict transforms; equality of their test sequences is precisely what permits applying the marked-ideal construction at every admissible stage.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; local presentations and replacement of the marked-ideal leading entry.

proof.text: On a finite affine cover, the heads and their tail words have finite images, so their union is finite. At a maximum head, its presentation identifies its stratum with the relevant marked-ideal cosupport. Upper semicontinuity of the head makes the maximum head closed; upper semicontinuity of the tail on that closed stratum makes the full maximum $T=\{\nu_H=m\}$ closed in $X_H$. Let $M_H$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each point of $T$ lies under a point of an etale neighbourhood $U\to X_H$ carrying a presentation; by Step 2, $\nu_H$ on $U$ is the word of that presentation, and the marked-ideal engine makes the preimage of $T$ the underlying set of a smooth closed center $C_U$ transverse to the exceptional divisors. The base change $M_H\times_{X_H}U\to M_H$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so $M_H\times_{X_H}U$ is reduced [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] with the same underlying set as $C_U$, hence equals $C_U$ by the uniqueness clause (3). Now $C_U$ is smooth over $\mathbf Q$, so its local rings are regular [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]. Etale maps are flat [def-weil-etale-morphism], so each local ring of $M_H$ maps flatly and locally to a regular local ring of $C_U$ and is regular [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular]. Thus $M_H$ is a nonempty regular closed subscheme when $X_H$ is singular. No maximum greater than $\bot$ meets the regular locus. Every generic point of a reduced scheme has a field as its local ring: localization at a minimal prime is reduced with only its zero prime, so each nonzero element is invertible. Thus a closed subset of singular points contains no irreducible component and hence no nonempty open subset. This proves the claimed nowhere density.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11 and local maximum-locus gluing; generic-point argument written out.

proof.text: Each affine coordinate ring of $X_H$ and $P_H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. A closed subscheme ideal is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Every submodule of a finite module over such a ring is finitely generated and finitely presented by [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented]; applying this also to kernels of maps from finite free modules proves coherence of the two ideals. The center is smooth over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth]. The ambient blowup and reduced strict transform remain in the required class by [lem-trf-smooth-center-blowup-geometry]. At the selected maximum, either the head drops or it stays fixed and the tail maximum strictly drops by the marked-ideal engine. At other points the admissible-transform heads and tails cannot increase. The next positive global maximum is therefore strictly smaller.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11; Stacks 0FUT and affine Noetherian coherence for geometric consequences.

proof.text: For a smooth pullback and $y\mapsto x$, [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile] gives $h_y=\Lambda^s h_x$ and $q_y=q_x+s$, with $c_y=c_x$. Hence $\Delta^{q_y}h_y=\Delta^{q_x}h_x$. This uses the fibre-local dimension $s$ at this point and requires no constant relative dimension. The local presentation theorem and the marked-ideal engine give equality of the tail words under this pullback, including the ordered exceptional data. Consequently $\nu(y)=\nu(x)$ at each finite stage. The maximum center is smooth over $\mathbf Q$ by Step 4. Its inverse image is smooth over it, as a base change of the smooth ambient map [lem-pc-proper-base-change], hence smooth over $\mathbf Q$ [lem-trf-smooth-composition] and reduced [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal]; it has the same underlying inverse-image stratum. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives equality of its extended ideal and the reduced stratum ideal. If empty, its ideal is the unit ideal. Restriction is the same comparison on an open neighbourhood. Deleting an empty center adds no exceptional hypersurface and changes none of the local data.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13 and 2.3.5(i); normalized smooth comparison and equality of reduced ideals.

proof.text: Suppose two histories satisfy (3). Their local rings identify, so their heads agree. The local presentation theorem identifies the maximal-order presentation equivalence classes using exactly the strict-transform schemes and the ordered earlier center ideals. The numerical marked-ideal engine then gives equal tail words. The retained ideals matter even for an intrinsic identity blowup: they determine the same ordered exceptional information used by the presentations. Thus the functions agree. Their images, maxima and maximum subsets agree, and uniqueness of reduced induced structure identifies their center ideals. The comparison is independent of local choices, so computing it before or after the restriction or smooth pullback in the preceding step gives the same head, presentation class and word. This proves the stated compatibility for finite histories, without identifying distinct ambient schemes.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; intrinsic minimal-embedding comparison, retaining ordered ideals.

proof.text: Assume an infinite maximum-center process from one initial pair. Its heads cannot increase. By [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile] they can strictly drop only finitely many times, so there is an infinite tail with the same maximum head. On this tail use its finitely many local presentations. The marked-ideal process is exactly the engine process at that head, since Step 2 used its tail word and Step 3 its full maximum center. By [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine] this process terminates with empty cosupport; by [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations] this removes that head, a contradiction. Equivalently the engine's coefficient-dimension induction and terminal monomial case exclude the putative infinite constant-head tail. For a finite disjoint union use its finite cover and the same global maximum rule, so the same argument applies. The empty scheme and every regular scheme have no positive maximum and yield zero steps. This proves (4) for the very functions constructed above; no well-foundedness of an arbitrary ordered set is asserted.

source.place: VIII 2.3.11, stopping before cleanup; presentation reduction and marked-ideal termination.
